★★★ A HAND-WRITTEN JUMP TABLE, TAKEN AT RUNTIME — the closing witness for D-ASM-INTERIOR-LABELS-NOT-ADDRESSABLE-AT-AN-OFFSET, and with it D-ASM-SYMBOL-OPERAND-NOT-LOWERED and D-ASM-INDIRECT-BRANCH-SUCCESSOR-SET-UNSTATED. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-13 under qemu-aarch64: exit 42.

★★★ THE FINDING THIS FIXTURE EXISTS TO PROTECT IS A REUSE CLAIM, NOT A FEATURE CLAIM. Nothing new was built to make this file run. `SyntheticBlockSymbol{symbol, blockByteOffset}` already WAS the interior-symbol-at-an-offset model, shipping for C's computed-goto and dense-switch tables; `assemble()` already published `blockByteOffsets` for every function; ELF/PE/Mach-O already emitted interior symbols at `funcTextStart[fi] + blockByteOffset`; and both targets already declared the `lea` variants `["symbol"]` and `["symbol","blockref"]`. What was missing was the assembly front end's wiring to all of it — so this `.s` produces the SAME LIR operand shapes `mir_to_lir.cpp` emits for `&global` and `&&label`, and NO relocation kind had to learn what an interior label is (interiority lives in the SYMBOL'S VA, so every relocation here carries addend 0 and the existing ADRP+ADD / ABS64 formulas resolve it unchanged).

★★ WHAT ONLY A RUN CAN WITNESS, AND WHY A BYTE PIN WOULD NOT DO. The three table slots are byte-identical zeros in the object; every claim about them lives in the RELOCATIONS and in the interior VAs the linker computes. ✔MEASURED on the relocatable object: `.rela.data` carries three R_AARCH64_ABS64 rows at offsets 0/8/16 against three DISTINCT local symbols, and those symbols sit in `.symtab` at `.text` offsets 0x10 / 0x18 / 0x30 — inside `main`, not at its entry. A build that bound all three to the function start would have identical bytes in the table and would still be catastrophically wrong. This repo has a scar for exactly that shape (perfect bytes, runtime SIGSEGV from a missing x30 spill), which is why the assertion is an exit code.

★★ THE DISCRIMINATION IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. ✔MEASURED by rebuilding this same file with the slot offset changed: `#0` -> exit 10, `#8` -> exit 42, `#16` -> exit 20. Three offsets, three different arms, each the correct one. So the table is not merely 'a table that works' — each slot independently holds the right interior address.

★★ THE DATA HALF IS LOAD-BEARING TOO. `adr x1, tbl` and `adr x2, bias` are the `D-ASM-SYMBOL-OPERAND-NOT-LOWERED` case: before this cycle a `.s` could DEFINE data and never REFERENCE it, so the data-directive work had no runtime read-back at all. Here `bias` is defined, its address taken, its value loaded, and 37 + 5 = 42 is the exit code — the read-back is the answer rather than a side check.

★★ M6 CAME FREE, WHICH IS THE POINT OF A REFUSAL KEYED ON ITS MISSING INPUT. `br x0` was refused until today by `derivableIndirectSuccessors().empty()` — a condition, not a constant. The refusal site was NOT edited: it simply stopped firing once the front end could bind an interior label's address, and `addIndirectBr` needed no relaxation. The refusal is still reachable and still tested (a `.s` with an indirect branch and no address-taken label is refused, naming the missing binding).

⚠ NO x86_64 LEG HERE: this file is AArch64 assembly and names AArch64 registers, so it is not portable text — an x86 arm would be a second source file and a different example. The x86_64 half of this capability is its sibling `asm_x86_64_interior_label_indirect_branch` (interior-label address + indirect branch, which needs no data section), and the ENGINE's data-jump-table path is covered against the x86_64 TARGET in the unit tier (`tests/asm/test_asm_text_to_lir.cpp` declares the data directive rows on its fixture dialect and asserts the relocations and block-symbol bindings there). So the split here is about portable SOURCE TEXT, not about which CPU the mechanism reaches.

★★ RED-ON-DISABLE, i.e. what breaks this fixture and how: change the slot offset (`#8`) and the exit code changes to the named arm; delete a `.quad` row (the table shortens and the branch reads past it); bind every block symbol to its function start (all three arms become `main`, which loops or faults); drop the `.rela.data` ABS64 relocations (the slots stay zero and `br x0` jumps to 0); make `adr` emit `[symbol]` instead of `[symbol, blockref]` for an interior label (the symbol is never bound to a byte offset — measured as a mutant in `tests/asm/test_asm_text_to_lir.cpp`); remove the target's absolute-8-byte relocation row (`.quad Lzero` refuses, naming the width). The unit tier pins the two mutants that a corpus example cannot express.

★ THE `release` ARM, SCOPED HONESTLY. At the `encode` tier no MIR module exists, so the optimizer, the register allocator and calling-convention materialization never run — this arm does NOT witness the optimizer and cannot. It pins the narrower fact that `--config=release` still produces a working binary from assembly.
